answer: Rhythm-gated entry control. Each new identity must reach a vertex of activity through the jetty: a fixed sequence of interaction delays that no client can compress, so burst-created accounts stall at the gate. The rule enforces this traffic shape by rejecting any identity whose arrival intervals fall below the measured baseline, and a fable of fast onboarding cannot hide the wait. An attacker pays real wall-clock time and idle compute per identity, multiplying fleet cost by the enforced delay.
